scenario.title: Mars: A Light That Answers
scenario.premise: A damaged landing strands a small expedition. Recovery becomes a rescue, then a return journey carrying people and evidence. This is an engineering story with recovered qualified systems, not real survival instructions.

stage.title: A voice above the ridge
stage.speaker: Mission Control
stage.motivation: We lost your signal on landing. Repair the radio and put a powered signal above the ridge. We are listening.
stage.travelText: We take the useful equipment onward to a voice above the ridge, leaving the earlier work where it stands.

objectives.text: Place a powered radio or directed optical beacon on Contact ridge.

stage.title: The things we left behind
stage.speaker: Survey crew
stage.motivation: Before the drive failed we left a small furniture sled beside the route. We remember the way. Bring it back; it has our table and the pictures that made this camp ours.
stage.travelText: We gather the known equipment for this nearby work. The larger expedition remains at its current camp or depot.

things.label: Toolkit

locations.label: Cargo shoulder

cacheNarrative.narrative: The crew identifies its own tagged sled on a nearby known shoulder. Only ordinary recovery padding and their personal picture roll are new loose pieces; the crate unfolds into its original mess table.

things.label: Toolkit
things.description: The expedition’s service tools and diagnostic meter, suitable for inspecting the matched spare drive before fitting it.

things.label: Heater
things.description: The expedition’s compatible enclosed electric heater. It can warm the refuge or an existing food pouch.

things.label: Pressure patch
things.description: A qualified repair patch from the habitat kit, intended for the marked fabric seam damage—not for arbitrary pressure-vessel repairs.

things.label: Rover
things.description: A wheeled chassis is a recognizable rover with unfilled component slots.

things.label: Tow eye
things.description: The matching rated recovery attachment for the rope and rover.

things.label: Drive coupling
things.description: The matched mechanical connection between the serviced spare drive and this crawler.

things.label: Disabled crawler
things.description: The crew’s intact mobile cabin with a failed drive. Repair the drive, or tow the cabin along the gentle recovery route with the equipped rover.

things.label: Bedding
things.description: The crew’s clean folded bedding for their camp bed.

things.label: Soup pouch
things.description: An intact prepared meal from the crew’s stores. Warm it before putting it in the insulated flask.

things.label: Insulated flask
things.description: An empty food flask that will keep the warmed meal ready while the crew is brought to shelter.

things.label: Folding bed
things.description: A complete camp bed. It needs bedding before it will be a comfortable resting place.

things.label: Serviced drive
things.description: The replacement drive has passed its toolkit inspection. Its matched coupling still needs fitting.

things.label: Replacement drive
things.description: The inspected drive with its coupling attached, ready to replace the failed crawler unit.

things.label: Crawler
things.description: The original survey crawler with its failed drive replaced. Its cabin and occupants can reach the prepared refuge.

things.label: Warm refuge
things.description: The repaired shelter with its heater connected, ready to receive a proper resting place.

things.label: Prepared refuge
things.description: A warm shelter with a made-up bed inside, ready to receive the crew from the crawler.

things.label: Occupied refuge
things.description: The recovered crew are inside the prepared refuge. A hot meal will let them settle after the difficult wait.

things.label: Warm soup
things.description: The heated meal pouch, ready to transfer to the insulated food flask.

things.label: Secured cargo sled
things.description: Attach the sling to the sled’s designed handling points.

scenario.title: Mars: A Light That Answers
scenario.premise: A damaged landing strands a small expedition. Recovery becomes a rescue, then a return journey carrying people and evidence. This is an engineering story with recovered qualified systems, not real survival instructions.

stage.title: The things we left behind

stage.motivation: Before the drive failed we left a small furniture sled beside the route. We remember the way. Bring it back; it has our table and the pictures that made this camp ours.
stage.travelText: We gather the known equipment for this nearby work. The larger expedition remains at its current camp or depot.

args: I stopped voluntarily in episode 9 without reaching the crew portrait. This was fresh play only after an authored later checkpoint, not a full-campaign run or a claim about human players. The table and personal pictures were an appealing modest goal; I wanted to see the crew settled together. Padding the rope into a sling and securing the sled made sense after my initial padding-on-sled attempt failed. After that I could not find the intended recovery action. Placing the secured sled on the cargo shoulder only said Placed, with no progress. The secured-sled hint gave no combinations or settings. I carried it to Recovery camp, where its hint still gave none; I then looked for hauling equipment on the Survey recovery route. Crawler plus sled failed. I brought the rover and tow eye back, made and fitted a tow line, but rover plus secured sled also failed, and the rover hint gave no combinations or settings. Carrying the supposedly abandoned cargo freely between places while not recovering it was confusing. The trips and repeated empty hints became uninteresting; I stopped because I was hunting an unstated rule rather than acting on the appealing story. I would have continued if a concrete recovery affordance or explanatory response had kept that story moving. I do not know whether the blockage is the checkpoint, my misunderstanding, or the game rule, and I did not inspect hidden files.
